items.title: King receives Anwar at Istana Bukit Tunku
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, received Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim at Istana Bukit Tunku today. According to a post on Sultan Ibrahim's Facebook page, the King was briefed on the latest developments in the Federal Government's administration and discussed current issues with Anwar. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Trump denies he offered Iran sanctions relief, release of frozen funds
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump on Monday denied a report by the news outlet Axios that he offered Iran sanctions relief and the release of frozen funds, as the Mideast war drags on. "Axios just released a story that 'Trump' offered Sanctions Relief and Frozen Funds to Iran. The Axios story reported that Trump "is willing to give Iran sanctions relief and release Iranian frozen funds in return for concrete Iranian steps regarding the nuclear programme."

items.title: Hazy conditions descend on Malaysia again as 31 areas hit ‘Unhealthy’ API
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — A total of 31 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as at 9 am today. According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, the areas included the Serian Police headquarters in Sarawak with the air pollutant index at 175; Pasir Gudang (170) and Larkin (169) in Johor; Bandaraya Melaka (166); Nilai, Negeri Sembilan (165); Johan Setia, Selangor (163); and Batu Muda in the capital (114). Thirty areas had a moderate API reading while seven areas had a good API reading.

items.title: HSS latest job win backs 70 sen target: Apex Securities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: HSS Engineers Bhd's latest contract win from Sutracom Sdn Bhd for engineering consultancy and site supervision at Indah Water Konsortium Sdn Bhd's (IWK) sewage treatment plant in Negri Sembilan is likely to contribute RM3.83 million in gross profit. Apex Securities said the contract adds to HSS' orderbook and reinforces its presence in the domestic water and wastewater segment. "Assuming a 35 per cent gross profit margin, we estimate the contract could contribute about RM3.83 million in gross profit over its tenure.

items.title: Sultan Nazrin: Malay community, Muslims facing adab crisis
items.summary: "The Malay community and the Muslim ummah are facing a crisis of adab," he said. Sultan Nazrin also expressed condolences to former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his family following the death of Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali. He said the 75th National Council for Islamic Religious Affairs Malaysia meeting conveyed its condolences to Dr Mahathir and his family.

items.title: 39pct of EPF members on track to meet basic savings target
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Nearly four in 10 active Employees Provident Fund (EPF) members in the formal sector are now on track to meet the basic savings benchmark of RM390,000 by age 60, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. However, Anwar said too many Malaysians remained at risk of outliving their savings during retirement, which could last between 20 and 25 years. Anwar said retirement adequacy remained a challenge as millions of Malaysians worked outside conventional formal employment, while the social protection system was largely designed around formal employment.

items.title: Former Felda Investment CEO charged with cheating board over RM500m Jalan Semarak land deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — A former chief executive officer of Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC) was charged in the Sessions Court here today with two counts of deceiving the company’s board of directors over the commercial development of Felda land along Jalan Semarak in 2014. On the first count, Zaid is accused of deceiving the FIC board into believing that Synergy Promenade Sdn Bhd was qualified for appointment as the project’s master developer, despite knowing the company was only eligible to serve as its master planner. On the second count, Zaid is accused of deceiving the FIC board regarding the commercial valuation of 24 lots of Felda land by misrepresenting that a market assessment by Firdaus & Associates Property Professionals Sdn Bhd valued the development at RM330.96 million, when the valuer's actual reported assessment was RM691.7 million.

items.title: Australia household spending is flat in August after strong run
items.summary: SYDNEY: Australian household spending was flat in August as consumers cut back on everything from food to clothing and culture, data showed on Tuesday, while they forked out more for fuel. The Australian Bureau of Statistics' monthly household spending indicator was unchanged in August at A$82.3 billion (US$57.71 billion). The annual pace of spending growth was still robust at 6.8 per cent, showing resilience to higher borrowing costs.

items.title: Marine police, Perhilitan seize RM700,000 worth of protected birds in Terengganu
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Sept 29 — The Kuala Terengganu Region Three Marine Police Force (PPM) and Terengganu Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) seized more than 50 protected birds and 60 cages worth RM709,950 in an integrated operation near Kampung Binjai Manis, Manir, here Sunday. PPM Region Three commander ACP Mohd Khairuddin Jamal said all the birds found during the operation yesterday afternoon were protected species under the Wildlife Conservation Act 2010 (Act 716). Khairuddin said the operation involved personnel from the Kuala Terengganu and Tasik Kenyir sectors of the Region Three Marine Police Force, as well as 14 Terengganu Perhilitan officers.

items.title: 'It is difficult to accept Tok is gone,' says Siti Hasmah's granddaughter
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali's granddaughter, Ally Mukhriz, expressed her grief over the loss of her grandmother, saying it was difficult to accept that she was gone. "We lost Tok (Dr Siti Hasmah) unexpectedly today (yesterday), and it is difficult to accept that she is gone," she said in an Instagram Story last night. Ally, whose real name is Meera Alyanna Mukhriz, thanked those who reached out to her and her family following the death of her grandmother, the wife of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad.

items.title: Police nab two men ‘chauffeuring’ 690kg of ketum in Toyota Alphard on NSE
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 29 — Two local men were arrested after allegedly possessing 690 kilogrammes of ketum leaves in a car at KM371 of the North-South Expressway (PLUS) southbound early yesterday. He said the two suspects were believed to be runners supplying ketum leaves for the local market. Khalid said preliminary checks found that the first suspect had one drug-related record and five criminal records, while the second had two drug-related records and one criminal record.

items.title: Ex-FIC CEO pleads not guilty to two charges over Felda land deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC) chief executive officer Mohd Zaid Abdul Jalil pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court today to two charges of cheating the company's board over a proposed commercial development of Felda land in Jalan Semarak. Zaid, 55, was accused of deceiving the board into believing that Synergy Promenade Sdn Bhd was qualified to be appointed as the project's Project Delivery Partner-Master Developer. MORE TO COME [[nid:1543541]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: PM lauds Malaysian contingent on best WorldSkills showing since 1995
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated the Malaysian contingent for winning one bronze medal and 13 Medallions for Excellence at the WorldSkills Competition (WSC) Shanghai 2026. Anwar said the achievement was the national contingent’s best performance in the competition since 1995. “Continue to hone your skills and pursue excellence.

items.title: Highways of the future
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's highway story dates back to March 1964, while toll collection was introduced two years later, in March 1966, on the Tanjung Malim-Slim River Highway, which, according to data from the Works Ministry, was the first highway in Malaysia and Asia. The highway construction sector subsequently expanded rapidly, particularly after the North-South Expressway was completed and opened to traffic. HIGHWAYS AS VITAL CONNECTORS Reflecting on the growth of Malaysia's highway sector, Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan said the country now has a 2,151-km highway network spanning 34 routes and operated by 28 concessionaires.

items.title: UK shop price inflation slows despite costs pressures
items.summary: The BRC survey showed: Annual shop price inflation fell to 1.4 per cent in September from 1.5 per cent in August but was slightly above the three-month average of 1.3 per cent. Food price inflation slowed to 2.5 per cent from 2.8 per cent as promotions helped bring down meat and dairy prices although poor harvests in Europe pushed up fruit prices and high commodity prices kept chocolate and confectionary prices elevated. Non-food inflation slowed to 0.8 per cent from 0.9 per cent as strong discounting reduced the cost of back-to-school essentials.

items.title: Single mother seeks help after fallen trees damage century-old family home
items.summary: KUALA KRAI: A single mother and her daughter were left shaken after their nearly 100-year-old family home in Kampung Chenulang here was damaged when two trees fell on it during a storm on Thursday. Rozilawani Mohamad Nor, 58, said the incident occurred at 6.10pm during heavy rain accompanied by lightning and strong winds. "Two trees, a bachang and a durian tree behind the house, fell and damaged the living room and bedroom.

items.title: Browser boom in trading
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Amid increasingly volatile and fast-moving financial markets, contracts-for-difference (CFD) trading is becoming more mobile and browser-based, with online platforms giving traders faster and more flexible access to global markets across devices, according to JustMarkets. Instead, users can access trading platforms through standard web browsers without configuring devices or meeting specific hardware and operating system requirements, the company said in a statement. JustMarkets said the key advantages included zero installation, cross-device flexibility, faster market access and integrated trading functionality.

items.title: Malaysia launches first phase of Rohingya repatriation to Myanmar
items.summary: LUMUT, Sept 29 — Malaysia began repatriating around 1,500 Myanmar nationals on Tuesday, launching the first phase of a return programme that has raised concerns from rights groups. The group is the first of 5,000 Myanmar nationals Malaysia says have agreed to “voluntary” repatriation from detention centres. Dozens of buses arrived under police escort at the Majlis Perbandaran Manjung stadium near the Lumut naval base in northwestern Malaysia, AFP correspondents saw.

items.title: Lahat landfill turns waste into renewable energy
items.summary: IPOH: Gas produced from the decomposition of solid waste at a landfill is being converted into electricity through a 2MW Biogas Renewable Energy Plant at the Lahat Sanitary Landfill here. The 2MW facility, the first sanitary landfill biogas project in northern Peninsular Malaysia, captures landfill gas for productive use while helping reduce greenhouse gas emissions, particularly methane, into the atmosphere. Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said the project demonstrated how landfills could be viewed not merely as waste disposal sites but also as potential sources of energy.

items.title: Gold holds near seven-week low, US economic data on tap
items.summary: LONDON: Gold steadied on Tuesday but hovered near a more than seven-week low on concerns that the Federal Reserve may keep interest rates higher for longer, while investors awaited a slew of US economic data. US gold futures fell 0.3 per cent to US$4,155.50. * Among other metals, spot silver fell 0.3 per cent to US$60.76, platinum steadied at US$1,717.70 and palladium was flat at US$1,214.75.

items.title: GOF seizes RM86,000 worth of firecrackers in raid, 40-year-old man arrested
items.summary: TEMERLOH: The General Operations Force (GOF) seized 49 boxes of firecrackers and fireworks worth RM86,700 during a raid on a store at Taman Bukit Bendera last night. GOF Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the man failed to produce any documents for the items stored there. "The firecrackers were believed to be leftover stock from the previous festive season," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Felda Investment ex-CEO to face charges today over KLVC project misappropriation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — A former chief executive officer (CEO) of Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC), investigated for alleged misappropriation involving the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project, is scheduled to be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court today. On Sept 25, MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman reportedly said the individual would face two charges under Section 417 of the Penal Code. According to Abd Halim, another individual, a former general manager of the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda), will face one charge under Section 420 of the Penal Code.

items.title: Ringgit opens slightly higher against greenback, major currencies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened slightly higher against the US dollar and a basket of major currencies on Tuesday, with elevated geopolitical risks continuing to favour defensive positioning. "Meanwhile, US Treasury yields moved sharply higher, with the two-year and 10-year yields hovering around 4.9 and 5.2 per cent, respectively," he told Bernama. Higher US yields reinforce the relative attractiveness of US dollar assets and could limit demand for emerging-market currencies, including the ringgit, he said.

items.title: Japan bond yields hold near multi-decade highs before 40-year auction
items.summary: TOKYO: Japanese government bond (JGB) yields held near multi-decade highs on Tuesday as inflation pressures set the scene for an auction of the market's longest-dated tenor. Here are a few details: * The benchmark 10-year JGB yield rose 0.5 basis point (bp) to 3.090 per cent, near the 30-year high of 3.115 per cent touched last week. Yields move inversely to bond prices.

items.title: Whistleblowers to get financial rewards for exposing cartels, says MyCC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — The Malaysia Competition Commission (MyCC) will strengthen protection and provide rewards to whistleblowers who provide information on cartel activities or bid-rigging practices, following amendments to the Competition Act 2010 (Act 712) and the Competition Commission Act 2010 (Act 713). MyCC chief executive officer Datuk Iskandar Ismail said stronger protection was crucial as cartel activities typically occurred secretly and behind the scenes, requiring the cooperation of whistleblowers connected to companies or consumers. He said the move would also make it easier for the public, particularly consumers, to lodge complaints regarding anti-competitive practices.

items.title: 27 areas record unhealthy API readings, Serian highest at 174
items.summary: In Negri Sembilan, Nilai recorded 164, followed by Port Dickson (155) and Seremban (152). In Melaka, Bandaraya Melaka recorded 164, followed by Bukit Rambai (161) and Alor Gajah (153). Cheras, Kuala Lumpur recorded 158, Putrajaya (154), while Rompin, Pahang recorded 152.

items.title: #NSTviral: 'Marrying me' - Dr M's playful quip about Siti Hasmah resurfaces [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An old video of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his late wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali, has resurfaced on social media. The quip drew a laugh from Dr Siti Hasmah, who was seated beside him. Near the end of the video, Dr Siti Hasmah playfully kissed Dr Mahathir on the cheek, drawing smiles from the host and audience.

items.title: Trump government ads draw scrutiny weeks before midterm elections
items.summary: NEW YORK: Taxpayer-funded television ads featuring President Donald Trump, including spots celebrating a "golden age of America" and one accompanied by a chorus singing "love me" on repeat, are drawing bipartisan criticism and legal questions five weeks before midterm elections. The three nationally broadcast ads, ending with the disclaimer "Paid for by the US Government," have prompted ethics experts and lawmakers from Trump's fellow Republicans and rival Democrats alike to question whether public funds are being used to promote the president politically. Critics say the campaign may violate longstanding restrictions on government propaganda and political activity, while the White House has defended the spots as "public service announcements" intended to promote patriotism rather than campaign ads.

items.title: Anthropic's IPO prospectus shows sweeping AI vision, surging costs
items.summary: Anthropic reported a net loss of US$42 billion in 2025, and plans to spend US$518 billion on cloud, computing and infrastructure obligations in coming year, according to the prospectus. Anthropic declined to comment. A US$2 TRILLION VALUATION EXPECTED Anthropic's expected valuation target is more than double its own estimated valuation of US$965 billion in May.

items.title: Russia pummels Kyiv in latest deadly daytime attack
items.summary: KYIV: Russian drones struck Ukraine's National Academy of Sciences in the historic heart of Kyiv on Monday, in the latest deadly daytime attack on the Ukrainian capital. Kyiv has increasingly faced Russian drones and missiles as Europe's worst conflict since World War II grinds through its fifth year. A Russian jet-powered drone struck a Ukrainian village near the Polish border earlier Monday, damaging a border checkpoint, a regional Ukrainian official said.

items.title: US stocks fall, bond yields rise as Middle East war drags on
items.summary: NEW YORK: Wall Street stocks retreated Monday as US Treasury yields continued to climb after US President Donald Trump rejected Iran's offer of a seven-day truce. Oil prices also rose, although crude finished well below session highs as traders were heartened that Trump also signaled he expects talks to continue. Markets also digested a report from Iranian state media that Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi was set to meet on Monday with Qatari mediators in New York.

items.title: Goldman's board has discussed plan to name John Waldron as next CEO
items.summary: NEW YORK: Goldman Sachs' board has discussed a plan for David Solomon to step down as chief executive and be replaced with chief operating officer John Waldron as soon as next year, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday, citing people familiar with the matter. Chief executive officer (CEO) succession has become a key focus for investors across Wall Street. Under the plan, Solomon would remain executive chairman for one to two years after stepping down from the CEO role, according to the report.

items.title: Politicians' pension reform needed to ensure fairness [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Issues revolving around the government's pension scheme are expected to rise again during the 2027 Budget debate. Pensions' payment allocated under the 2026 Budget — RM42.8 billion — constituted roughly 12.3 per cent of total federal government revenue. While it is important for the government to reform the civil service pension scheme, pundits are saying that reform of politician's pension schemes is needed in the spirit of fairness.

items.title: Negri Sembilan's growth story unfolds beneath political storm [WATCH]
items.summary: The state secured RM10.2 billion worth of construction projects as at Sept 15, surpassing the RM6 billion recorded throughout 2025, as industrial parks and data centres drive development. RHB Research said Negri Sembilan ranked sixth nationwide in construction project awards, behind Johor, Selangor, Sabah, Sarawak and Kuala Lumpur. CONSTRUCTION BOOM GATHERS PACE The value of construction work done in Negri Sembilan reached RM1.6 billion in the second quarter (Q2) of 2026, compared with RM1.2 billion a year earlier.

items.title: Iran: Qatar to give US new ideas to reopen Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Qatari mediators will present the US with new ideas discussed with Teheran on how to meet Iran's conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said late Monday, adding a final response from Washington could come Tuesday. Speaking to Iranian reporters in New York, Araghchi said he met again with Qatari mediators and discussed possible ways to facilitate implementation of Teheran's conditions, Anadolu Ajansi reported. Araghchi said he would leave New York for Teheran within hours and that the Qatari mediators would relay the US response once it was available.

items.title: Buying a strata home? The rules that can govern your pets, parking and even your access card
items.summary: Sarawak has its own Strata Management Ordinance 2019. In essence, the SMA provides for the management and maintenance of strata buildings and their common property, while setting out the rights and responsibilities of homeowners and management bodies. They cover everyday issues residents may encounter, including nuisance, pets, vehicles, common facilities, security and unpaid charges.

items.title: Early intervention key to helping distressed students, says Dzulkefly
items.summary: THE Health Ministry is stepping up preventive measures and strengthening school-based mental health support to address suicidal behaviour among students, particularly where bullying is a factor. Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry was working with the Education Ministry to improve counselling services, early detection and intervention for students showing signs of distress. Dzulkefly said the ministry would also deploy its Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Services team to assist affected students, schools and communities.

items.title: Pope urges Europe to help combat 'lies and deceit' in world affairs
items.summary: METZ, France: Pope Leo XIV warned on Monday that relations between nations were becoming increasingly uncivilised with people boasting of "lies and deceit", urging Europe to help break the spiral and foster respect in international ties. Instead, people boast of lies and deceit," Leo said in French, alongside President Emmanuel Macron and a handful of other leaders. "Sadly, war has returned, even to Europe," he said.

items.title: 'More fine-tuning is needed'
items.summary: THE Freedom of Information (FOI) Bill needs comprehensive improvements before it is finalised, said Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said yesterday. She said her ministry was conducting a study covering the practical aspects and implementation mechanisms across various levels of the government. Speaking at the National Town Hall on the Freedom of Information Bill at Parliament, Azalina said a good law must go beyond good intentions.

items.title: After 70 years together, Dr Mahathir weeps as Dr Hasmah laid to rest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — After seven decades together, Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad today faced one of his most difficult moments as he accompanied his late wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, to her final resting place. To Malaysians, Dr Mahathir and Dr Siti Hasmah were not merely a former prime minister and his wife. Dr Mahathir and Dr Siti Hasmah tied the knot on August 5, 1956 and last August marked their 70th wedding anniversary.

items.title: Perak seeks RM1.4b in Budget 2027 for key water infrastructure
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 28 — Perak is hoping for at least RM1.4 billion in the upcoming Federal Budget to fund key water supply infrastructure, particularly a project to transfer water from Sungai Perak to Bukit Merah to support farmers regularly affected by drought. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said the project was among the state’s priorities submitted by the Perak Economic Planning Unit to the Finance Ministry ahead of the Budget announcement. He said the project would involve two main components, with the first involving infrastructure such as pumps and water tunnels.

items.title: Dr Hasmah laid to rest at National Mausoleum as crowd of supporters gather in droves to pay last respects
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 28 — The remains of the late Tun Dr Hasmah Mohd Ali have been laid to rest at the National Mausoleum in Precinct 20, Putrajaya. Dr Mahathir with family members during the burial. He said he also wanted to offer his condolences to Tun Dr Mahathir, whom he described, together with Dr Hasmah, as leaders who understood the rakyat.

items.title: Bank Negara: Malaysia’s financial markets remain orderly amid global headwinds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Malaysia’s domestic financial markets continued to adjust in an orderly manner, supported by balanced two-way flows that ensured effective price intermediation among market participants, according to Bank Negara Malaysia’s Financial Markets Committee (FMC). The FMC also said recent movements in the domestic financial markets were driven primarily by global factors, particularly developments in the US policy rate. This came amid a broader repricing of global interest rate expectations and higher global bond yields.

items.title: From violin to rural medicine, 10 things Malaysians may have forgotten about Dr Hasmah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — It is easy to remember Tun Dr Hasmah Mohamad Ali through the people and institutions around her: as the wife of Malaysia’s longest-serving prime minister, as a former First Lady, or as the woman who stood beside Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad through decades of public life. As tributes pour in following her death at 100, here are 10 details that offer a glimpse of the Dr Hasmah that could have been missed by public eyes. Dr Hasmah recalled working with Unicef to train traditional midwives in cleaner and safer practices.

items.title: Hundreds gather at Seri Kembangan mosque to pay final respects to Dr Hasmah
items.summary: Her husband, former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, arrived in a separate vehicle travelling alongside the hearse carrying his wife’s remains. Former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad arrives at the As-Syarif Mosque in Seri Kembangan on September 28, 2026. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, arrived around 4pm to pay their respects to the bereaved family.

items.title: Released earlier this year, Federal Court now orders two men back to jail for cannabis trafficking
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 28 — Two men released from prison earlier this year must return to serve the remainder of their original 30-year sentence, after the Federal Court reinstated their convictions for trafficking 264.36 grammes of cannabis. “We find there was overwhelming evidence of trafficking as found by the trial court,” he said. The Federal Court reinstated the 30-year jail term that the High Court had imposed on both men on Oct 20, 2023.

items.title: JPJ cracks down on foreign drivers, 481,119 summonses issued from 2024 to Sept 2026
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 28 — A total of 481,119 summonses were issued by the Road Transport Department (JPJ) against foreign drivers through the special operation codenamed ‘Ops Khas Pemandu Warga Asing’ (PeWA) from 2024 to September this year. JPJ senior enforcement director Datuk Muhammad Kifli Ma Hassan said the main offences detected were not possessing a Competent Driving Licence, expired Motor Vehicle Licence and no insurance coverage. He said that foreigners are not allowed to apply for vocational licences such as Goods Vehicle Licence and Public Service Vehicle Licence, therefore employers need to ensure that lorry or bus drivers meet all the stipulated requirements.

items.title: Civil servant, ex‑CEO plead not guilty to RM18,000 gold mining graft charges
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 28 — A civil servant and a former chief executive officer today pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here to three corruption charges involving RM18,000 in bribes allegedly linked to facilitating gold mining operations in Sabah. According to the charges, Chong allegedly gave Robert cash loans of RM10,000 in April 2024, RM3,000 in October 2024 and RM5,000 in October 2025 as an inducement to facilitate the company’s gold mining operations. Robert was separately charged under Section 17(a) of the MACC Act 2009 with corruptly obtaining the three cash loans from Chong to facilitate the company’s gold mining operations, with the same penalties under Section 24(1).

items.title: Fahmi tells telcos: Rethink diesel gensets, embrace renewables for tower operations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — The government has called on telecommunications companies to reassess their reliance on diesel generator sets (gensets) to operate some 60,000 telecommunication towers nationwide, particularly in rural areas. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the large-scale use of fossil fuels to keep telecommunication towers operational needed to be gradually reduced by switching to renewable energy sources, in line with the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR). “There are about 60,000 telecommunication towers nationwide.

items.title: Sabah police advise against gospel band Israel & New Breed concert over public sensitivities, two reports lodged
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 28 — Sabah police have advised that a band named Israel & New Breed’s planned concert here in October not be held for now, citing public sensitivities and concerns over public order. Sabah Police Commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun said police had received two reports concerning the concert, which has been widely publicised on social media. However, he said the main consideration for police was public sensitivity and maintaining public order.

items.title: Malaysia’s passport now No. 2 globally, sharing silver tier with Singapore
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 28 — The Malaysian passport is now ranked second globally in The Passport Index Global Ranking 2026, rising from third last year. “Based on the ranking, Malaysian passport holders have access to 175 destinations, comprising 129 visa-free destinations and 46 destinations with visa-on-arrival, while 23 destinations require a visa,” according to the post. Based on data from www.passportindex.org, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) passport holds the top spot in the Passport Power Rank, followed by Singapore and Malaysia in second place.

items.title: Lee Chong Wei mourns Dr Hasmah: ‘To us, she was a warrior’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Badminton legend Datuk Seri Lee Chong Wei has paid tribute to Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, remembering her as a “warrior” and a source of affection for the national squad, following her death today at the age of 100. Lee said her love for badminton “never faded”, and that he had not realised it would be their last conversation. But to me and the entire national badminton squad, Tun was a warrior, the person we respected most,” he said.

items.title: Singapore Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong recalls Dr Hasmah’s humour, zest and love for music
items.summary: SINGAPORE, Sept 28 — The late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah was a warm and gracious person, full of life, and had a wonderful sense of humour, said Singapore Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong. Dr Siti Hasmah, wife of former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, passed away at the National Heart Institute (IJN), Kuala Lumpur on Monday morning at the age of 100. “Ho Ching and I will remember Tun Siti Hasmah fondly,” he said in his Facebook post on Monday.

items.title: HEAL 15555 crisis line records 267,873 calls for counselling, intervention since Covid‑19 pandemic
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 28 — The National Mental Health Crisis Line (HEAL 15555) has intervened in 518 behavioural crisis cases over the past four years, covering suicidal ideation and suicide attempts. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said that of that figure, 347 cases were of suicidal ideation. He said of that total, 220,856 clients (82 per cent) received emotional support assistance, while 47,014 clients (18 per cent) received specific intervention by counselling psychology officers.

items.title: Religious teacher pleads not guilty to sexual assault charges involving 16‑year‑old boy in Ipoh
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 28 — A religious teacher, known as an ustazah, at a national secondary school was charged at the Sessions Court here today with three counts of physical sexual assault against a 16-year-old male student two years ago. The accused, Haslina Abu Bakar, 48, however, pleaded not guilty to all charges read before Judge Ainul Sharin Mohamad. According to the first charge, the accused is alleged to have committed physical sexual assault by kissing the boy on the mouth for sexual purposes in November 2024.

items.title: Fahmi: Dr Hasmah to be laid to rest beside Endon Mahmood at National Mausoleum
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — The remains of the late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali will be laid to rest beside the tomb of Tun Endon Mahmood, the late wife of Malaysia's fifth prime minister Tun Abdullah Ahmad Badawi. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil disclosed this while sharing the funeral arrangements, after paying his respects at Dr Hasmah's family residence in Seri Kembangan earlier this afternoon. “My wife told me that she (Dr Siti Hasmah) spoke a lot about God.

items.title: Tabung Haji opens Haj appeals Oct 2, earlier start gives pilgrims more prep time
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Tabung Haji (TH) will open appeals for the 1448H/2027 Haj season via the THiJARI application and website from Oct 2, a month earlier than in the previous season. TH Group managing director and chief executive officer Mustakim Mohamad said the earlier opening would give prospective pilgrims more time to prepare financially, physically and in terms of their knowledge of the Haj. “The Haj payment for pilgrims selected through the appeal process is the full Haj cost of RM33,300 for the 1448H/2027 season, in line with the concept of istito’ah in fulfilling the obligation to perform the Haj.

items.title: Elderly woman found stabbed to death in Menglembu, daughter with psychiatric history held
items.summary: Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the 70-year-old victim was found with a stab wound to her chest and was believed to have been killed by her daughter, who has a history of mental health treatment. He said police received a report from the victim’s son-in-law at about 7pm. Mohd Alwi said police also seized a knife believed to have been used in the incident.

items.title: Major city roads, highways to close this weekend for KL Marathon 2026
items.summary: They include Jalan Raja, Jalan Raja Laut, Jalan Dang Wangi, Jalan Munshi Abdullah, Jalan Ampang, Jalan Sultan Ismail, Jalan P. Ramlee, Jalan Raja Chulan, Jalan Kuching, Jalan Kinabalu and Jalan Sultan Hishamuddin. From 11.00pm on Saturday, Jalan TAR, Jalan Tun Perak, the AKLEH, MRR2 and the northbound DUKE Highway towards Jalan Duta will also shut. Jalan Sultan Ismail is expected to reopen at 6.30am, Jalan Tunku Abdul Rahman at 9.00am, and Jalan Tun Perak and Jalan Dang Wangi at 9.30am.

items.title: Thunderstorm warning in effect for Pahang, Sarawak and Sabah until 5pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for parts of Pahang, Sarawak, and Sabah, with heavy rain, gusty winds, and lightning expected to persist until 5pm today. In Sarawak, the alert covers the Bintulu division (Bintulu and Sebauh), Miri, and the Limbang division. In Sabah, the warning covers a wider area, encompassing Tawau, the Sandakan division (Tongod, Telupid, Kinabatangan, and Sandakan), the Interior division (Sook, Keningau, Tambunan, Membakut, and Pensiangan), alongside the West Coast division and Kudat.
